newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BANK CLB SERVES THIRD OF CLIENTS VIA PHONE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BANK CLB SERVES THIRD OF CLIENTS VIA PHONE.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Belgium (CLB), a unit of French Credit Lyonnais, said on Tuesday that a third of all its client contacts in Belgium were handled via its Brussels call center.
"We expect the percentage of telephone contacts will rise to 50 percent by the end of the century and to 66 percent by the year 2005," CLB retail director Yves Delacollette told a news conference.
A client calling one of CLB's 30 regional branches is automatically diverted to the Brussels call center, where 45 employees can handle all banking transactions.
"Everything can be done by phone," Delacollette said.
He added that only about 15 percent of the incoming calls were forwarded to the regional offices.
The call center -- the only one operated by a Belgian bank -- is open from 0700 to 1900 local time.
Delacollette said CLB does not inform its clients that their calls are diverted to a call center, but does not hide it from them either.
"If you tell people beforehand that their call will divert to Brussels, they will not call," he said.
Delacollette said that CLB's telephone investment advice service is used by 0.5 percent of its 220,000 customers, but that 0.5 percent represents five percent of funds managed.
CLB also sells mortgage loans by telephone since the end of last year. CLB distributes the loans, which are produced by Argenta, a small Flemish bank.
